# The Solution · FinWise

> Module 2 · Acquisition & Activation. The onboarding solution and the Aha moment that makes value land.

## Aha moment

I can see my real cash position and what’s coming in the next 30 days, without doing any work.  The user sees their own connected bank data, auto-categorized, with a short-term cash-flow forecast and one specific insight, such as “You’ll dip below $5k around Nov 12” or “3 invoices worth $8,400 are overdue.”

Why this one:

It uses their own data. Small business owners don’t care about a demo dashboard. They care about their 
money. Generic value doesn’t convert at 2%; personal value can.
It answers the question every small business owner worries about: “Am I going to be okay this month?”
It can be reached in minutes. A bank connection plus auto-categorization delivers it with almost no manual input. Invoicing or payroll setup can’t.
It fits the reverse trial. The forecast and insights should be premium features. That way the user feels the loss when the trial downgrades, which is the whole mechanism of a reverse trial.

2–3. The flow: 3 screens

Screen 1: Personalize (quiz)

Job: Make the Aha screen relevant to their situation.
Action: Answer two tap-only questions: business type and “What’s your biggest money headache right now?” (cash running low / chasing invoices / no idea where money goes / tax time).
The answer decides which insight leads on Screen 3. Two questions, no typing, under 15 seconds.

Screen 2: Connect your bank

Job: Get the real data that makes Aha possible.
Action: Connect one bank account.
Lead with the payoff, not the mechanism. “See your next 30 days of cash” works better than “Link your account.”
Pre-sort the bank list by region, with the most common SMB banks first.
Fallbacks for people who won’t connect: CSV upload, or a clearly labeled sample business. Sample data gets them to a preview of Aha, not the real thing, so follow up later to get the connection.

Screen 3: Your cash picture (the Aha)

Job: Deliver the moment. The user sees their current balance, a 30-day forecast, and one insight matched to their quiz answer.
Action: Act on the insight with one tap: “Send reminder for overdue invoices” or “Turn on low-cash alerts.”
That action is what brings them back, and return visits are what drive conversion.
Badge the forecast and insights as premium (“Included in your trial”) so the downgrade later feels like a loss.

4. Where personalization and pre-filling shorten the path
Where	Tactic	What it saves
Sign-up	Google or Intuit SSO; pull business name from email domain or firmographic enrichment	Removes a profile screen entirely
Screen 1	Infer business type from enrichment and pre-select it, so the user only confirms	Cuts the quiz to about one tap
Screen 2	Pre-sort banks by location and business type; offer import if they arrive from QuickBooks or Xero	Fewer search steps, fewer drop-offs
Screen 3	Choose the leading insight from the quiz answer; auto-categorize everything	Removes setup work, and the user’s first view is already relevant

Metrics to track: % of sign-ups reaching Screen 3, median time to Screen 3 (aim for under 3 minutes), drop-off at Screen 2 (the bank connection is the main point of friction), and Day-7 return rate. If Screen 2 drop-off is high, A/B test whether moving the sample-data preview before the bank ask lifts connection rates.

## Why this activates

the prototype makes a user feel the product working on their money before they’ve done any work, then gives them a reason to come back, and the reverse trial turns that into something they’ll miss. To be clear, this is the hypothesis behind the design, and it still needs to be tested against your data
